01 IWAE RESEARCH WORKFLOW
IWAE FIELD GUIDE / 2026
From Evidence
to Insight
A practical workflow for turning source material into
connected, reviewable knowledge without losing its origin.
READ
Inspect the source at
full fidelity.
CAPTURE
Lift only the evidence
you need.
CONNECT
Arrange claims into a
visible argument.
The core promise
Every idea remains inspectable: you can see what it means, where it came
from, and how it supports the work around it.
Self-authored sample document for testing selection, search, capture, and source tracing. 1 / 6

02 IWAE RESEARCH WORKFLOW
A Reading Workflow
A useful research note preserves the claim, the surrounding context, and a direct route back to the source.
01
Orient
Scan the outline, identify the author's purpose, and mark the section
that answers your current question.
02
Capture
Select the smallest passage that still contains the claim, its
qualifier, and the words needed to interpret it.
03
Connect
Place the excerpt near related evidence, then add a short note that
states why the relationship matters.
04
Verify
Return to the source before publishing. Confirm wording, page
location, and whether later evidence changes the claim.
Self-authored sample document for testing selection, search, capture, and source tracing. 2 / 6

03 IWAE RESEARCH WORKFLOW
Capture Meaningful Evidence
Capture only enough material to preserve meaning; the smallest useful excerpt is easier to compare and reuse.
Selection quality test
Read the excerpt without looking at the page. If the subject, claim, or
limiting condition becomes ambiguous, expand the selection by one
sentence and test again.
Good evidence is concise, but never context-free.
SIGNAL TOO LITTLE USEFUL CAPTURE
Claim Result only Result plus subject
Constraint Number only Number plus condition
Definition Term only Term plus defining
sentence
Exception Warning only Rule plus exception
Self-authored sample document for testing selection, search, capture, and source tracing. 3 / 6

04 IWAE RESEARCH WORKFLOW
Keep Context Attached
An excerpt is valuable because it can be checked. A source link should survive
movement, resizing, translation, and visual rearrangement.
A durable source anchor stores
Document identity
Page and selected geometry
Exact quoted text
Text before and after the quote
SOURCE TRACE
Page 4
Excerpt block
Trust rule
Keep source identity, page location, selected geometry, and quoted text
together. If one part changes, the link should be treated as stale rather
than silently trusted.
Review cue
When a source moves, show uncertainty. Never repair a citation by guessing
silently.
Self-authored sample document for testing selection, search, capture, and source tracing. 4 / 6

05 IWAE RESEARCH WORKFLOW
Synthesize on the Canvas
Spatial arrangement turns a list of quotations into an argument you can inspect.
QUESTION
What does the
evidence support?
SOURCE A
Direct
observation
SOURCE B
Limiting
condition
CLAIM
A bounded
conclusion
A SMALL, EXPLICIT NOTE IS ENOUGH
question -> evidence
evidence -> interpretation
interpretation -> reviewable claim
Use proximity for grouping and visible connectors for claims that must remain
explicit.
Self-authored sample document for testing selection, search, capture, and source tracing. 5 / 6

06 IWAE RESEARCH WORKFLOW
Review Checklist
Before a note becomes a decision, draft, or published explanation, test whether
another reader can retrace the reasoning.
OK
SOURCE
Can every excerpt return to its document and page?
OK
CONTEXT
Does each capture include the qualifier that changes its meaning?
OK
STRUCTURE
Can the reader tell which evidence supports, limits, or contradicts
the claim?
OK
LANGUAGE
Are your own words visually distinct from quoted material?
OK
REVIEW
Did you revisit the original source after arranging the final
argument?
Evidence is useful when it remains understandable, connected, and verifiable.
Self-authored sample document for testing selection, search, capture, and source tracing. 6 / 6
